publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. There is continuing interest in the use of visible-emitting AlGaInP-GaInP quantum well lasers in optical information storage systems, optical pumping of solid-state laser media and short-haul communication systems employing plastic fibers. In these applications ability to operate at high temperatures is important, nevertheless it is well known that there is a strong thermally activated contribution to the threshold current of these devices at room temperature and above, which in 670-nm devices is thought to be due to the leakage of electrons through the p-cladding layer. We have modelled 670-nm devices with two 6.8 nm GaInP compressively strained quantum wells.

articleTitle: Excimer laser machining by a multiple imaging system using holographic optical elements
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We propose excimer laser machining using a multiple imaging system employing a holographic optical element (HOE). The multiple imaging system can generate many images from one mask pattern. The HOEs that we used were computer-generated phase holograms, the so-called kinoform type. Their diffraction efficiency can theoretically reach 100%.

articleTitle: The effect of beam interaction time on laser cladding process
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In the laser cladding process, a molten pool of the pasted or blown powder with a complex three-dimensional shape is formed on the substrate, by the laser beam interaction with powder material. This interaction time plays a crucial role for the desired successful cladding. In our present analysis, we find that in a narrow range of power density and beam interaction time, the regime of laser cladding could further be classified for evolution of coarse, fine, and ultrafine dendrite microstructure.

articleTitle: Chirp limitation on high-speed wavelength conversion using semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The use of wavelength convertors in multiwavelength optical networks can enhance network flexibility. Cross-phase saturation effects in semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) have been used in interferometric arrangements to achieve noninverted conversion with chirp compression and high extinction ratios. However, successful operation of such devices requires careful control of the drive conditions. Furthermore, their high-speed low-chirp operation, requiring large signal and cw powers, must avoid gain saturation, which counteracts the noninverted interferometric conversion. This paper considers the chirp introduced on conversion, employing crossgain saturation, and studies its dependence on amplifier drive current and signal power. It further shows how an increase in injected cw optical power can reduce chirp while improving conversion speed.

articleTitle: An actively mode-locked, 10-GHz, single-polarization, picosecond erbium fiber laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have developed an actively mode locked laser that utilizes intracavity nonlinear pulse compression to produce a completely filled pulse train with a pulse duration of 1.24 ps at repetition rates in excess of 10 GHz. The laser is driven by an external oscillator allowing it to be synchronized to a master clock in an optical-fiber communications system. The components of the laser are either polarization-maintaining (PM) or are birefringence-compensated, making the laser insensitive to environmentally induced birefringence variations.

articleTitle: Synchronization of environmentally coupled, passively mode-locked fiber lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Synchronization of mode-locked lasers has become a subject of increasing interest lately due to the utilization of ultrafast lasers in communications systems, pump-probe measurements, and other applications. Commercial systems have been developed for synchronizing mode-locked Ti:sapphire lasers to an external source or to other mode-locked lasers. Here, we report the synchronization of two passively mode-locked Er:fiber lasers to an accuracy of 5 psec RMS.

articleTitle: 3-D low-coherence imaging for multiple-layer industrial surface analysis
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In conclusion, this system may provide useful information about reflecting interface layers inside transparent objects, at micron scale over a virtually unlimited range. In spite of the 8-bit intensity resolution and 56-dB dynamic range of the CCD camera, which theoretically limit the number of detectable air-glass interfaces to about 80, good images have been obtained in both cases. This method could be especially beneficial for applications where the object features are difficult to access by direct physical measurement such as in assessing the surface roughness of a paint layer under a clear lacquer coating.

articleTitle: Non-Bragg diffraction orders in highly efficient photorefractive polymers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Photorefractive polymers have improved considerably in recent years. Due to their higher processing capabilities compared with inorganic photorefractive crystals and their high efficiency and sensitivity they appear as promising new materials for photonic applications. Due to high refractive index modulations that can be achieved in DMNPAA:PVK:ECZ:TNF guest/host photorefractive polymers, we recently demonstrated with these polymers a variety of optical applications including holographic storage and dynamic holographic interferometry with low-power laser diodes in a four-wave mixing geometry. In this paper, we demonstrate that the recording of thick phase holograms in these polymers leads not only to very efficient Bragg diffraction but also to strong diffraction into non-Bragg orders. These non-Bragg orders have features drastically different from those of Raman-Nath diffraction orders on thin gratings.

articleTitle: Infrared image studies of diode-pumped Yb/sup 3+/, Er/sup 3+/:glass
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Laser emission at 1535 nm from an Er/sup 3+/:glass laser is very useful due to its eye-safe wavelength and high transmission through fiber optics and the atmosphere. Diode pumping allows for considerably greater quantum efficiency, dramatically decreasing the thermal design constraints. Recent technological advances in the manufacture of InGaAs laser diode arrays have brought commercial laser diodes, in the wavelength range of 900 to 1000 nm, to market from several manufacturers. This wavelength range matches the strong Yb/sup 3+/ /sup 2/F/sub 7/2/-/sup 2/F/sub 5/2/ transition, making it an ideal pumping source for Yb/sup 3+/, Er/sup 3+/ glass. In this paper we report the initial results of experimental studies using an infrared image camera to map the Yb/sup 3+/ and Er/sup 3+/ fluorescence in a side-pumped, Er/sup 3+/:glass laser configuration. Two laser diode arrays of 1 cm length have been used in our experiments.

articleTitle: High-average-power kilohertz sub-100-fs amplifier
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated a sub-100-fs Ti:sapphire-based amplifier system capable of producing over 5 W of average power at 1-kHz repetition rate, which was the highest reported power to our knowledge. This 5-fold increase of power will open up more opportunities for researchers in nonlinear frequency conversion, biological and medical imaging, and more.

articleTitle: Dynamic grating formation in As/sub 2/S/sub 3/
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. This work focuses on using the photoexpansion effect to fabricate surface-grating structures and studying their applicability in photonic circuitry. Surface gratings with periods ranging from 2.95 /spl mu/m to 0.377 /spl mu/m were written holographically using 514.5-nm light from an argon ion laser. Gratings with 2.95 /spl mu/m period were also written for different exposure times to study the dose effect on surface-relief structures. Atomic force microscope (AFM) images of the irradiated surfaces were obtained. A He-Ne laser operating at 632.8 nm was used to measure diffraction efficiencies.

articleTitle: cw and high-repetition rate Nd:YAG laser with nonlinear cholesteric liquid crystal mirror
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In the present paper, we report for the first time in our knowledge about some restrictions of using cholesteric liquid crystal (CLC) adaptive mirrors in high-repetition-rate short-pulse lasers because of the possibility of nonlinear bleaching of CLC mirrors. In cw operation CLC mirrors with lower misalignment sensitivity than conventional dielectric ones were successfully used by our group in Nd:YAG laser resonators.

articleTitle: Ultralow threshold current lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Ultralow threshold current vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) will enable practical laser-based smart pixels. Such devices have emerged through the application of monolithically integrated native oxides of AlGaAs as current constriction and mode control layers and as high-contrast Bragg reflectors. In this paper we will demonstrate and analyze the role of the oxide in current constriction and optical field control to predict the scaling of VCSELs to microamp thresholds. In addition, we will demonstrate and analyze the impact of high-contrast AlAs oxide/GaAs Bragg mirrors formed by selective oxidation on the performance of VCSELs and study the tradeoffs in device characteristics that arise from use of electrically insulating mirrors.

articleTitle: High-average-power, long-pulse-length solid-state illuminator laser for high-resolution imaging
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have recently reported a laser amplification technique that allows pulses of up to 1 /spl mu/s in duration to be efficiently generated from a master oscillator power amplifier (MOPA) geometry. The incorporation of very low threshold SBS phase conjugation using Brillouin-enhanced four wave mixing provides near-diffraction limited divergence and the output pulses can be frequency-doubled to 527 nm with >50% total external conversion efficiency. We have applied this technology to a high-average-power laser system designed as an illuminator for high-resolution speckle imaging (HRI) of distant objects through the turbulent atmosphere. The laser incorporates four flash lamp pumped Nd:glass zig-zag laser amplifers.

articleTitle: High-performance liquid-based passive optical limiter
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Our studies reveal that cells made of high-grade fused silica containing Zn:tetra(p-methoxyphenyl) tetrabenzporphyrin (TBP) in solution in tetrahydrofuran (THF) have a very high damage threshold fluence close to that of the bare fused silica. Other materials, such as Si:naphthalocyanine, in toluene exhibit considerably lower damage thresholds. For this reason, and because of the large nonlinear absorption of TBP, we chose this combination of materials to fabricate a tandem nonlinear optical limiter using TBP.

articleTitle: Sub-50 femtosecond, multiterawatt Ti:sapphire laser system
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Recent advances in ultrashort (<100 fs) pulse lasers have made it possible to explore ultrahigh field physics using relatively compact laser systems. We report on the design and construction of a compact Nd:LiYF/sub 4//Ti:sapphire-based chirped pulse amplifier (CPA) system capable of producing over 750 mJ in pulses shorter than 50 fs at 1 Hz. This system is composed of a Kerr-lens mode-locked Ti:sapphire laser oscillator.

articleTitle: Compact blue upconversion fiber laser pumped by a diode-pumpable Raman fiber
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Compact and rugged blue laser sources are needed for a wide variety of commercial applications. The thulium-doped ZBLAN fiber laser, which has yielded over 100 mW of blue, appears particularly suitable for such applications. Unfortunately, because of the present unavailability of high-power diode lasers at the appropriate pump wavelengths (1110-1150 nm), scalability of such lasers to higher powers in a reliable and cost effective manner remains a significant problem. This talk demonstrates such a scalable pump source, and its use as a pump for an unoptimized Tm:ZBLAN fiber laser. Our work is based on the use of a Raman fiber laser as a novel pump scheme for the 480-nm Tm:ZBLAN upconversion fiber laser.

articleTitle: Fluorescence detection of biological aerosols
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The application of two-dimensional spectral analysis to microbes and other biological particles suspended in the atmosphere requires laser excitation in the ultraviolet spectral region. Much of the previous study on spectral characterization has been restricted to bulk samples of biological materials. In this study, a KrF excimer laser at 248 nm was used to carefully determine absolute fluorescent cross sections, while a tripled Cr:LiSAF laser, tunable from 265 to 290 nm, was used to obtain excitation-emission matrix (EEM) profiles. The higher intensity of tunable laser sources is critical to investigating biological material in aerosol form.

articleTitle: Crystal growth of Cr,Ca(Mg):Y/sub 3/Al/sub 5/O/sub 12/ with high Cr/sup 4+/-doping concentration
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. When chromium is doped into Y/sub 3/AlO/sub 12/ (YAG), it substitutes for aluminium and normally occupies octahedral sites as Cr/sup 3+/. However, the active center giving 1.35-1.6-/spl mu/m emission is Cr. Therefore, obtaining high concentrations of Cr and to therefore improve the NIR absorption, Cr/sup 4+/+ is the key to grow Cr-doped YAG crystals. Cr:YAG, Cr,Mg:YAG and Cr,Ca:YAG crystals were grown by the CZ method with various Cr and Ca concentrations.

articleTitle: Passively aligned laser array to silica-on-silicon waveguides with 36% coupling efficiency and 30 mW cw coupled power
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In conclusion, we have demonstrated a passive alignment technique that allows p-down mounting of an array of laser diodes to a silica-on-silicon photonic integrated circuit. This packaging method is particularly well adapted for WDM transmitter or receiver arrays where an active array of lasers or detectors can be inexpensively coupled to a mux or demux silica-on-silicon circuit.

articleTitle: Bleaching effect in nanosized chromogenic WO/sub 3/ under picosecond excitation
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We report on the nonlinear optical effects on WO/sub 3/ nanoparticles embedded on polyvinylalcohol thin film. Picosecond pump-probe technique (15-ps pulses at 540 nm from Nd:YAlO/sub 3/ laser as pump and 15-ps white continuum as probe) was used.

articleTitle: Longitudinal-mode control in Fabry-Perot lasers by focused ion beam etching
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In principle a 'made-to-measure' spectrum through laser mode sculpturing can be realized without significant increases in threshold current using this novel focused ion beam etching (FIBE) system where control of both position and depth of the etched trench is incorporated with in situ monitoring.

articleTitle: Beam combination of parallel semiconductor laser amplifiers by photorefractive coupling
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Recently, SDL Inc. integrated several amplifiers in a parallel way to get a diode master oscillator power amplifier (MOPA) array with a coherent laser output. In this presentation we propose and demonstrate a diode laser MOPA system using photorefractive multibeam coupling to combine amplifiers in phase.

articleTitle: CsLiB/sub 6/O/sub 10/ crystal: growth and properties
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Interest in borate crystals for ultraviolet (UV) nonlinear optics (NLO) has increased because all solid-state UV lasers obtained by NLO are strongly requested. Much effort has been spent on developing borates series in the 1990s. Recently the borate crystal, CsLiB/sub 6/O/sub 10/ (CLBO), has been discovered and developed by the present authors. In this talk we report on growth, doping, and NLO properties of CLBO.

articleTitle: VCSELs with nonuniform multiple quantum wells for a very wide temperature range of CW operation
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The temperature range over which CW operation of vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) exhibit a low current threshold can be extended by broadening the gain spectrum. This can be achieved through the use of nonuniform multiquantum wells (MQWs) in the active region, which allows the lasing mode to be aligned to the gain peak over a wider range of temperatures. To achieve efficient lasing operation, it is essential that the gain of each quantum well be sufficiently high to compensate for the reduced gain contributions from other wells at the lasing wavelength. This is easily satisfied at lower temperatures, where the differential optical gain is significantly increased and the quantum efficiency is high (>80%). We have previously demonstrated efficient CW lasing operation at cryogenic temperatures (6 K to 250 K) using a VCSEL with uniform multiple quantum wells that achieved optimal gain-mode alignment at /spl sim/100 K. By use of multiple quantum wells of different thicknesses (nonuniform MQWs), and thereby obtaining a broadened gain spectrum, the CW performance of the laser has improved and the overall temperature range of operation has increased.

articleTitle: Local surface deformation analysis by photothermal method
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. During the past few years a great deal of attention has been focused on the development of photothermal methods in order to characterize the thermal properties of solid samples. In this work the harmonic local surface deformation induced by a Gaussian pump laser beam modulated in time is studied through the photothermal method by the direction change of a second laser beam (probe) reflected by the bended surface.

articleTitle: Selective oxidation of integrated optical elements
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Selective oxidation of AlGaAs compounds allows formation of Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ layers embedded in unoxidised semiconductor material. It is known that the oxidation rate depends very strongly on the Al concentration. By vertically tailoring Al mole fraction in such a way that upon selective oxidation from the side of the exposed mesa, oxide-semiconductor interface penetration into the semiconductor follows a desired dependence in the vertical direction integrated optical elements can be formed.

articleTitle: Pulse shaping of incoherent light by use of a liquid crystal modulator array
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We apply femtosecond pulse shaping techniques for electronically programmable phase filtering of broadband incoherent light at 15 /spl mu/m. Pulse shaping applied to incoherent light results in tailoring of the electric field coherence function. In contrast to the pulse intensity and phase profile, as in the usual coherent femtosecond pulse-shaping experiments. A standard fs pulse shaper was introduced in one arm of a Michelson interferometer. Pulse shaping was achieved using a liquid crystal modulator.

articleTitle: Blue and blue-green lasers by intracavity sum-frequency generation with potassium niobate
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Modulated blue and blue-green light sources are strongly desired for a wide variety of applications. Recently, an efficient intracavity sum-frequency mixing (1064 nm+910 nm/spl rarr/490 nm) in a b-axis KNbO/sub 3/ crystal was demonstrated by using Ti:Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ laser and a Nd:YVO/sub 4/ laser pumped by a 400-mW laser diode. In this paper, the possibility of all-solid-state blue-green and blue lasers of 10-mW class was demonstrated by the intracavity sum-frequency generation (1064 nm+860 nm/spl rarr/475 nm, 1064 nm+780 nm/spl rarr/450 nm, 1064 nm+690 nm/spl rarr/418 nm) using KNbO/sub 3/ crystal, and the direct-modulation characteristics were examined.

articleTitle: Tunable high-power AlGaAs distributed Bragg reflector laser diodes
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Commercial single-mode distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) laser diodes now produce output powers comparable to commercial single-mode Fabry-Perot laser diodes. Within this presentation, high-power tunable AlGaAs DBR laser diodes with single-mode output powers exceeding 200 mW cw are described. In addition, an 16,000 hr. ongoing lifetest on DBR laser diodes will be presented. These results represent over an order of magnitude increase in the output power of tunable DBR laser diodes and excellent proof that regrown AlGaAs laser diodes can have exceptional reliability.

articleTitle: Coherent antiStokes Raman spectroscopy using a tunable optical parametric oscillator injection-seeded by single-mode diode lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Coherent antiStokes Raman spectroscopy (CARS) is performed on nitrogen gas (N/sub 2/) using the tunable signal wave from a pulsed optical parametric oscillator (OPO) based on /spl beta/-barium borate (BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/). The continuously tunable output frequencies and optical bandwidth of this OPO are controlled by injection seeding at the idler wavelength with single-mode radiation from an external-cavity diode laser (ECDL).

articleTitle: High-average-power 1.54-/spl mu/m Er/sup 3+/:Yb/sup 3+/-doped phosphate glass laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper describes our achievement of a laser with an average output power of 20 W at 1.54 /spl mu/m and a slope efficiency of 4 % based on our detailed investigation on pump dynamics, thermal behavior, and long-pulse laser performance of this new glass material. To our best knowledge, this is the most powerful and efficient lamp-pumped Er:glass laser to date.

articleTitle: Kerr-lens mode locking without dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We propose and theoretically investigate an alternative approach to Kerr-lens mode-locking (KLM), which avoids the group velocity dispersion (GVD) compensation by use of a negative net nonlinear refractive index per cavity round trip. For the compensation of the positive nonlinear refractive index of the laser crystal we propose to utilize a nonresonant bulk semiconductor inserted in the tightly focused resonator section.

articleTitle: THz oscillations in the optical emission of a semiconductor microcavity
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The ultrafast optical emission of semiconductor microcavities has attracted considerable interest recently. Reported observations include coherent vacuum Rabi oscillations after weak resonant optical excitation, the emission of single pulses after nonresonant optical pumping, and relaxation oscillations after electrical pumping. We report here the first investigation of femtosecond time-resolved emission from a semiconductor microcavity resonantly excited with intense femtosecond pulses.

articleTitle: A novel technique to improve the performance in optical amplifier WDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We proposed a novel technique of nonlinear suppression using nonlinear suppression lights (NSL), and confirmed the improvement of the system performance in a long-haul optical amplifier system. It is important to load the NSL with proper wavelength and level in order to obtain the best system performance. For example, this technique is applicable to improve system performance for the constructed system. In addition, NSL is useful to adjust the optical power per channel in WDM systems.

articleTitle: Coherence, stability and localization resistance of extended two dimensional vertical cavity locked laser arrays
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Experiments were performed with laser arrays based on InGaAs-GaAs quantum well laser structure with epitaxially grown Bragg mirrors. The arrays were fabricated by spatially modulating the top laser mirror reflectivity, by the deposition of highly reflecting metal on the laser elements, and less reflecting metal on the interlasers part of the array, forming a quasi-gain-guided array. Theoretical modeling was based on the rate equation approximation of the 2D coupled semiconductor laser array. For the coherence analysis we dwelled with the phase equation around the steady-state solution, while for the stability analysis the complete set of variables; amplitude, carriers, and phase, were tracked. The transfer of coherence was examined by formulation of the small signal transfer function.

articleTitle: Design, fabrication, and characterization of the double-barrier, reservoir, and quantum well electron tranfer modulator
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We present data of an enhanced version of the BRAQWET, where an additional 70-/spl Aring/ InP barrier layer has been added between the reservoir and the quantum well. This additional barrier serves to increase the confinement of the wavefunction to the quantum well. For this reason we refer to this new structure as DBRAQWET, to signify the presence of a double barrier. Optical simulations employing a Poisson-Schrodinger self-consistent scheme shows clearly the increase in absorption and the accompanying increase in differential absorption.

articleTitle: Molecular beam epitaxy regrowth of top reflectors for multiple wavelength vertical cavity laser arrays
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have fabricated novel multiple wavelength vertical cavity surface-emitting InGaAs QW DBR (VCSEL) arrays employing molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) regrowth of the top distributed Bragg reflector (DBR). The individual emission wavelength of each laser element in the 2D array is set by anodic oxidation and selective etching of the wafer before regrowth.

articleTitle: Epitaxial lift-off for wafer-scale GaAs-on-Si semi-monolithic integration
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have developed a manufacturable epitaxial lift-off process to integrate a 2" GaAs epi-layer containing active photonic devices onto a much larger 5" processed Si VLSI wafer. The availability of this ELO hetero-integration process will be extremely valuable in high-performance and reliable optoelectronic integrated systems.

articleTitle: Generation of femtosecond X-ray pulses via Thomson scattering of terawatt IR laser pulses with relativistic electrons
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Generating femtosecond X-ray pulses via Thomson scattering of ultrashort laser pulses with relativistic electrons has a number of attractive advantages over other approaches. The duration of the generated X-rays is determined by the focal spot of the electron beam and the optical pulse duration. Thus generation of X-ray pulses of <100 fs duration is relatively straightforward. Furthermore, the X-rays are highly directed and of relatively narrow bandwidth. Finally, the Thomson scattering source of ultrashort X-ray pulses is also tunable, either by changing the angle of incidence between the electrons and photons, or by changing the laser photon energy, or by changing the electron beam energy. This source of ultrashort X-ray pulses promises to be a very useful tool in the study of the ultrafast atomic motion in solids and molecules.

articleTitle: Cancellation of B-integral accumulation in CPA lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We report the cancellation of B-integral accumulated in a regenerative amplifier by using a GaAs plate that has negative nonlinear index of refraction at 1.053 /spl mu/m. The nonlinear index of refraction is about three orders of magnitude larger than Nd:glass or KDP so a thickness of less than 1 mm is required. We show the compressed pulse duration measured as a function of accumulated B-integral increases without the compensator plate as B exceeds 1, while with the GaAs plate installed, the pulse duration remains fixed. 1.053-/spl mu/m chirped pulses are generated in a Nd:LiYF/sub 4/ laser oscillator coupled into a 0.8-km single-mode fiber. They are subsequently expanded in a grating pair.

articleTitle: 670-nm MOPA (diffraction-limited) diode pumping of the saturable Bragg reflector-mode-locked Cr:LiSAF femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In the present paper, we discuss scaling to high output powers without using higher pump powers. This is particularly important for the gain media in the fluoride material system that exhibit low thermal conductivity, and even more so for gain media that exhibit nonradiative processes that decrease power rapidly as temperature rises, such as Cr:LiSrAlF/sub 6/. The recent arrival of diffraction-limited high-power laser diodes has made possible increases in pumping efficiency. We evaluate the suitability of the red diffraction-limited laser diode for use in a saturable Bragg reflector (SBR) mode-locked Cr:LiSrAlF/sub 6/ laser.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of femtosecond pulse propagation in air undergoing self-focusing and ionization
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Intense, ultrashort laser pulse propagation in gases is of considerable current interest. Recently, self-channelling of femtosecond pulses in air over 20 m in distance has been demonstrated. To better study the propagation characteristics of such pulses, we have developed a numerical code based on the paraxial wave equation.

articleTitle: High-gain amplification in a liquid phase epitaxial Nd:YAG waveguide
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. There is a growing appreciation of the possibilities for high-gain amplification in solid-state laser materials pumped by high-average-power diode lasers. So far the emphasis has been on bulk materials, however planar waveguides offer significant benefits. Their geometry is compatible with that of the diode laser and the confinement allows much smaller pumped volumes and hence higher gain for a given pump power. For example, with the Nd:YAG waveguide laser we have used the pumped volume is one order of magnitude smaller than could be achieved in a bulk medium of the same length.

articleTitle: Simple technique for measurement of the Raman gain in optical fibers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Our technique directly gives the Raman gain without requiring a tunable probe, calibration or absolute measurement of Raman signal. We send intense square shaped pulses near 1550 nm into 1 length of fiber and measure the stimulated Raman signal as a function of pulse duration.

articleTitle: Fiber grating laser: An alternative configuration
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In conclusion, we have shown that it is possible to obtain increased output power from a fiber grating laser (FGL) that uses a high reflectivity grating (in this case from the rear facet of the device).

articleTitle: Comparative photothermal study of singleshot and multishot laser damage on UV multilayers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. A photothermal two-probe-beam setup measuring the temperature as well as the displacement at the sample surface was used for single and multishot experiments. UV-laser pulses of 20 ns pulsewidth at a wavelength of 248 nm heat a sample.

articleTitle: Impact of the residual facet reflectivity on beam profile filamentation in semiconductor laser amplifiers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper we elaborately apply the beam propagation method (BPM) to allow for the more appropriate superposition of the optical fields in the InGaAs-GaAs QW active semiconductor laser amplifer device. With the inclusion of the lateral phase variations we are able to study the impacts of residual facet reflectivities on the performance characteristics of traveling wave amplifiers in detail.

articleTitle: Raman spectroscopy of semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper reports micro-Raman scattering investigations on GaInP/AlGaInP, GaAs/AlGaAs, and strained InGaAs/AlGaAs single quantum well (SQW) graded-index separate-confinement heterostructure ridge lasers. It demonstrates the potential and usefulness of Raman spectroscopy for optimizing the performance and reliability of laser diodes by measuring (i) local mirror temperatures, (ii) mechanical stress fields, (iii) mirror lattice disorder, and (iv) mirror coating stability under laser operation. Raman spectra have been measured in the backscattering geometry on the (110) facets of the 5-/spl mu/m-wide lasers by using the 457.9 nm Ar+ laser line with low powers of /spl sime/1 mW focused on a 1-/spl mu/m spot size. In this geometry only the transversal-optical (TO) phonon modes are allowed.

articleTitle: Continuous wave 355-nm all solid-state laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Sum frequency mixing between the fundamental and second harmonic of Nd:YAG lasers yields 355 nm output. We report on generation of 410 mW of 355 nm output by doubly resonant sum frequency mixing.

articleTitle: Direct electronic tuning of a Ti:sapphire laser with an acousto-optic crystal
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In this work, an electronic frequency tuning of a Ti:sapphire laser over more than 100 nm has been achieved with a computer-controlled acousto-optic tunable filter (AOTF) and dispersion-compensation optics. Fast and random-ordered wavelength selection of individual output pulses have been demonstrated. The pump laser is a frequency doubled Q-switched Nd:YAG laser.

articleTitle: Design of a mid-IR active imaging system for gas detection using a pulsed laser source
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Backscatter absorption gas imaging (BAGI) is a remote sensing technique that uses active imaging to generate real-time video images of chemical vapor plumes. As such, BAGI represents a fusion between absorptive chemical detection LIDAR and imaging laser radar. Plume imaging occurs when a gas that can absorb light at the laser wavelength enters the system field-of-view, thereby attenuating the scene backscatter and causing a cloud image.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic generation in biased GaAs/AlGaAs quantum well
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Second-harmonic susceptibility of asymmetric or electrically biased GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells (QWs) can be exploited to realize frequency-conversion devices in the near-infrared. The calculated /spl xi//sup (2/) values associated with interband transitions are in the range of 10-20 pm/V. In this paper we have measured the /spl xi//sup (2/) in biased symmetric QWs, where the QW nonlinearity can be electrically switched on and off, so that synchronous detection of second harmonic (SH) generated by the QWs alone can be performed.

articleTitle: Microcavity enhancement of organic electroluminescent devices
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper describes a microcavity organic LED, which has enhanced spatially integrated and forward surface-emitted intensity, and which could be suitable for low information content display applications. The device employs an optical microcavity to enhance the efficiency of a nearly monochromatic organic light-emitting diode.

articleTitle: 1.55-/spl mu/m distributed feedback lasers for wide temperature range and high bit rates
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In summary design improvements of 1.55-/spl mu/m MQW DFB laser diodes will allow us to soon realize low-cost coolerless 2.5 Gbit/s transmitters with standard performance.

articleTitle: An air turbulence compensated interferometer: IC manufacturers' metrology needs translated into system component requirements
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. A new interferometric system has been developed, which is designed to meet the needs of high-end IC manufacturing in the immediate future. High-precision positional measurements during the lithographic exposures for IC manufacturing are critical to the ability to fabricate fine geometry circuits at high yield. The positional measurements are provided by high-performance interferometers, which are limited in performance principally by the turbulent air inside the lithographic exposure tool (a stepper). These turbulent-air-induced positional errors typically have a magnitude in the range of 10 to 100 nm. Our new system is a combination of the conventionally used HeNe-based interferometer system and a second colinear system based on second-harmonic interferometry (SHI).

articleTitle: New gratingless wavelength-stabilized laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Wavelength stabilization is usually obtained in semiconductor lasers with a diffraction grating close to the gain region. Generally this requires complex lithography and at least one regrowth step. Furthermore, the light from a standard semiconductor laser is highly elliptical and cannot efficiently be coupled to an optical fiber. Frequently, the total power output is limited by catastrophic mirror damage that occurs when the optical field becomes excessive at the semiconductor-air interface. We describe a novel structure that may overcome these problems of standard semiconductor lasers. The GaAs-AlAs QW laser is composed of two coupled waveguides, a thick low index waveguide and a lower semiconductor waveguide made with quarter-wave mirrors.

articleTitle: Dual wavelength operation of a self-seeded, triple-cavity type, pulsed dye laser oscillator
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. As the active medium, we have used a solution of rhodamine 6G in ethanol. We have used two 2,400 grooves/mm holographic gratings to obtain only the zeroth- and first-order diffracted beam. The incidence angle to the grating was about 880. We have used partially reflecting mirrors as feedback mirrors at both ends.

articleTitle: A cw tunable infrared spectrometer based on the difference-frequency generation in AgGaS/sub 2/ in the 5-/spl mu/m region-applicability for line broadening investigations and trace gas detection
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. A cw tunable infrared spectrometer based on the difference-frequency generation (DFG) in a nonlinear crystal AgGaS/sub 2/ (l=25 mm, noncritical type I phase matching) was constructed. The system was designed for the wavenumber region around 1900-2100 cm/sup -1/. In this spectral region the molecular gases like, CO, N/sub 2/O, and NO, have pronounced absorption lines excluding interferences from the major atmospheric gases.

articleTitle: Incomplete phase conjugation through a random phase screen
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The technique of optical phase conjugation can be used to reconstruct a laser beam that has been aberrated on passing through a distorting medium. Reflection from a phase-conjugate mirror (PCM) produces a time reversed replica of the aberrated beam. The aberrations are removed when this phase-conjugate beam propagates back through the distorting medium, producing a time-reversed replica of the original beam.

articleTitle: Influence of an external mechanical force on light emission from strained 1.3 /spl mu/m semiconductor lasers: polarization switching and mode spectra
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The polarization of light from strained semiconductor lasers can switch between TE and TM polarization in dependence on the strain in the active layer and the injection current. Experimental investigations of this effect give insight into the nonlinear interaction between differently polarized cavity modes. We have presented systematic experimental and theoretical investigations of the influence of strain on the emission properties of 1.3 /spl mu/m InGaAsP-InP ridge waveguide lasers by applying an external mechanical force.

articleTitle: Femtosecond time-resolved stimulated emissions in ZnSe thin film studied by up-conversion at room temperature
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Semiconductor ZnSe and its heterostructure materials can be developed as blue color light-emitting diodes, lasers and high-speed optoelectronics devices. The investigation of emission time evolution in ZnSe can provide important information for the understanding of emission mechanism and the improvement of the device characteristics. In this paper, we studied the temporal behaviors of stimulated and spontaneous emissions in ZnSe thin film by using time-resolved sum-frequency technique (upconversion) in the femtosecond region.

articleTitle: Diffraction from photorefractive gratings in quarter-wave semiconductor mirrors
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We present a novel device, a quarter-wave semiconductor mirror, which yields similar theoretical diffractive performance without the insertion loss associated with asymmetric Fabry Perot (ASFPs). A quarter-wave mirror operates in a high reflectivity region and does not require the careful control of surface quality and Fabry-Perot resonance placement necessary for the MQW ASFP. The device is similar in construction to stratified volume holographic optical elements except that it consists of alternating quarter-wave optical thickness layers of a nonabsorbing spacer and a photorefractive material.

articleTitle: Wafer-fused vertical-cavity bistable device at 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelength
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated a new vertical-cavity bistable device which exhibits all-optical switching at 1.55-/spl mu/m wavelength, with submilliwatt threshold and large contrast ratio. It was realized by wafer fusion of an InGaAsP/InP active heterostructure onto a AlAs/GaAs Bragg mirror. Finally the carrier-induced dispersive nonlinearity of the InGaAsP active layer has been investigated.

articleTitle: Self-compensating laser-based ultrasound sensor using integrated photo-induced EMF detection and time-delay interferometry
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Laser ultrasonics offers a technique for nondestructive, noncontact ultrasonic inspection. Progress has been made, which may enable this novel diagnostic to find its way into the manufacturing arena. We describe a novel technique, which may result in a compact, high-bandwidth low-cost laser based interferometric ultrasonic receiver.

articleTitle: Broadband compact mode-locked Er/Yb:fiber laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We discuss the design and operation characteristics of dispersion-compensated fiber laser that uses a short Er/Yb:fiber with a semiconductor 1550-nm saturable Bragg reflector. This laser is suitable for the chirped-pulse WDM application.

articleTitle: Soliton mode-locking for ultrashort pulse generation with slow saturable absorbers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. It is well known that mode-locked lasers will yield pulses that are both shorter and more stable if solitonlike pulse shaping is used, i.e., self-phase modulation (SFM) and negative group velocity dispersion (GVD) are properly adjusted. We extend these results and found a new mode-locking technique. Based on soliton perturbation theory we show that in a passively mode-locked femtosecond solid-state laser with solitonlike pulse shaping the mode locking process can by stabilised by only a slow saturable absorber.

articleTitle: A collimated beam of MeV electrons accelerated by a terawatt laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The field at the focus of a short-pulse, high-power laser is so high that electrons oscillate at nearly the speed of light, giving rise to several interesting, and previously unstudied, effects. For instance, it produces extremely high laser pressure (called the ponderomotive force), which can drive a high-amplitude plasma "wake-field plasma wave", the basis for what is called the laser wake-field accelerator (LWPA). We have recently demonstrated that a laser wake field can produce a collimated beam of MeV electrons and that the laser may have been guided by relativistic self focusing and electron cavitation.

articleTitle: The graphic arts industry in the year 2000 and beyond
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The laser is considered a key enabling technology for print production. Right now it is impossible to discuss the technological side of output for printing without including laser devices. Lasers have been used in output devices for over twenty years in the field of printing. The majority of these were low power gas lasers or laser diodes for exposing silver halide film, but recently there has been an increasing trend toward using high-power lasers for printing. The reasons for this are that the print production work flow has been dramatically shortened, and in addition to that, increased importance is being placed on more environmentally friendly production. To address these changes, the printing industry is now starting to use other technologies, which can be grouped, into two major categories. The first is the use of thermal sensitive film rather than silver halide film. This eliminates the chemical processing required for developing and fixing film. The second is a process that eliminates intermediate materials like film altogether such as or for example directly imaging onto the final aluminum printing plates. With these technologies, imaging is done by using optics to expose a photopolymer coating on the plates or by using heat to expose thermal sensitive plates.

articleTitle: Regenerative pulse-shaping techniques and their applications on the amplification of sub-20 fs or two-color femtosecond pulses
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In summary, we have successfully demonstrated a variety of methods to dramatically increase the bandwidth of Ti:sapphire chirped-pulse laser amplification systems. These methods have been used to generate amplified pulses as short as 18 fs. Additionally, we have simultaneously amplified and compressed two femtosecond pulses separated by as much as 100 nm in wavelength.

articleTitle: All-fiber 3/spl times/3 acousto-optic switch
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have previously made an all-fiber 2/spl times/2 acousto-optic switching element from a fused coupler. Here we describe a similar 3/spl times/3 switch. Two of three identical fibers are narrowed (pre-tapered) by different amounts, before all three are fused and elongated together to form the coupler. If the three diameters are sufficiently different, the result is a "null" coupler; light of any wavelength entering in a particular fiber will leave the coupler from the far end of the same fiber.

articleTitle: Modeling and characterization of erbium:ytterbium glass waveguide lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Erbium-ytterbium (Er/sup 3+/-Yb/sup 3+/) codoped glass is an attractive system for short, efficient lasers and amplifiers operating in the long-haul telecommunications range. The pump absorption near 980 nm is increased, and efficient energy transfer between the Yb/sup 3+/ and Er/sup 3+/ ions enables the operation of compact laser devices with low erbium concentrations. We present simple methods that can be used to model the Er/sup 3+/-Yb/sup 3+/ codoped glass system and predict laser performance. Experimental results for fabricated waveguide laser devices are discussed.

articleTitle: Latest innovations in high-power CO laser technology and outlook for the future
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper deals with the latest achievements on high-power, room-temperature operation of CO laser, which has long been thought as the breakthrough for the practical industrial applications of CO laser such as laser beam welding. Both a transverse-flow and a fast-axial-flow rf-discharge-excited CO lasers are now being optimized for room temperature operation. A steady output of more than 1 kW is achieved under nonoptimized conditions. Future outlook of the CO laser is also given.

articleTitle: Doppler lidar measurement of height profiles of turbulent-energy dissipation rate
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The method of measurement of turbulent energy dissipation rate in the boundary layer of atmosphere was developed. This method was tested using ground-based CO/sub 2/ cw Doppler lidar of Institute of Optoelectronics of German Aerospace Establishment in the fall of 1995 near Oberpfaffenhofen (Germany). The example of height profile of turbulent energy dissipation measured by Doppler lidar is presented.

articleTitle: Characteristics of asymmetric quantum well heterostructure lasers and amplifiers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Theoretical consideration by rate equations has shown that regimes of regular pulse generation at two or three remote optical wavelengths in the range of 790 to 850 nm can be realized in the GaAs-AlGaAs systems with bi- or triple quantum well heterostructure at suitable configuration and doping of active and barrier layers. Light pulse duration reaches values about 50 to 100 ps. Transformation of gain bands for TE and TM modes is dependent on the excitation current has been studied and calculations have been performed for the five quantum well GaAs-AlGaAs system.

articleTitle: Utilization of a commercial optical parametric oscillator for water vapor differential absorption lidar measurements
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We present measurements of the spectral characteristics of the commercially obtained optical parametric oscillator (OPO) (Continuum model Mirage 800) that reflect its suitability as an on-line differential absorption lidar (DIAL) transmitter.

articleTitle: Ultraviolet picosecond pulses from an all-solid-state Ce:LiSAF/Ce:LiCAF master oscillator and power amplifier system
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated the simplest, all-solid-state, UV short pulse Ce:LiSrAlF/sub 6//Ce:LiCaAlF/sub 6/ master oscillator power amplifier (MOPA) system pumped by the fourth harmonics of a conventional Q-switched Nd:YAG laser.

articleTitle: Near-infrared semiconductor lasers for gas analysis operating in the 2-/spl mu/m range
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Gas monitoring applications using semiconductor lasers, operating in the 0.7-2.0 /spl mu/m near-infrared (NIR) wavelength region, is a fast growing area with large potential. We will present semiconductor laser measurements of ammonia and carbon dioxide in the 2-/spl mu/m wavelength region, using the wavelength modulation spectroscopy (WMS) technique. Estimations of the improved detection limits and the problems with interfering absorption lines will be discussed.

articleTitle: Electroluminescent displays
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper will review the electrical and optical properties of thin-film electroluminescent (EL) displays. An electrical model for thin-film electroluminescent (TFEL) device operation will be presented and used to describe the luminance and power in TFEL devices. The luminance-voltage characteristics of a typical TFEL device are shown. The physics responsible for device threshold, charge transport, and optical emission phenomenon will be reviewed.

articleTitle: Multiwavelength optical power-limiting amplifier and its applications in a SONET WDM self-healing ring network
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In summary, we have presented the first multiwavelength optical limiting amplifier (OLA) with high dynamic range to our knowledge, and demonstrated its applications in a SONET WDM self-healing ring optical fibre network.

articleTitle: Spectral dynamics of widely tunable four-section sampled grating DBR lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Wavelength tunable semiconductor lasers are important components for use as optical transmitters in wavelength-division multiplexed communications systems. A promising structure to provide wide range tuning at 1.55 /spl mu/m is the four-section sampled grating DBR laser.

articleTitle: High-power FEL based on seeded single-pass amplifier using prebunched electron beams
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. A high-power, mirrorless free-electron laser (FEL) approach based on seeded single-pass amplifier with a prebunched high brightness electron beam as a high-gain medium is presented. This approach depends on a high-current density produced by compressing the electron bunch containing a few nanocoulombs to a few picoseconds. The high-brightness beam can be focused to a small spot, resulting in a very high current density.

articleTitle: High-speed formation of persistent gratings in doped semiconductors
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We describe time-resolved measurements of optical grating formation in Te-doped AlGaAs. Local refractive index modulation resulting from spatially selective ionization of defect sites known as "DX" centers produces holographic diffraction gratings with efficiencies above 10% for grating periods as small as 135 nm. These gratings are persistent for a duration that ranges from microseconds to many years depending on the sample temperature--the longer times being available only at cryogenic temperatures thus far.

articleTitle: Picosecond optical parametric oscillation in bulk quasi-phase matched lithium niobate
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) is an attractive nonlinear medium on account of its very large effective nonlinearity and the fact that with suitable period it can provide noncritical phase-matching for generation of any wavelengths in its transmission range. Here we report the first (to the authors' knowledge) operation of a PPLN synchronously pumped optical parametric oscillator.

articleTitle: Fourier-mode of open resonator with uniform amplitude on one reflector
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. A novel open-resonator lowest-loss mode with uniform output amplitude distribution is produced by an intracavity Fourier transform and inhomogeneities on one of the cavity mirrors. This mode is called Fourier-mode because its amplitude distribution functions at the end mirrors are approximately Fourier transforms of each other. Using the Fourier optics method, the integral equations describing the oscillation modes in the circular cross section of the generalized confocal resonator (GCR) with flat mirrors and with an amplitude-phase spatial filter on one of the reflectors are obtained taking into consideration the aperture finiteness both of the reflectors and phase corrector.

articleTitle: Resonantly enhanced difference-frequency mixing in the Lyman-alpha region
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We are pursuing improved vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) conversion efficiency by taking advantage of two-photon resonances within the tuning range of the ArF excimer laser. Difference-frequency mixing ArF and dye lasers can theoretically produce continuously tunable VUV from 110 to 180 nm with relatively high powers. We are pursuing this technique to generate tunable radiation in the region of Lyman /spl alpha/ at 121.6 nm. VUV light is generated by focusing beams from synchronized ArF and dye lasers into a mixing cell.

articleTitle: Compact high-resolution holographic storage
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. In summary, we have proposed and demonstrated a lensless, high-resolution ROM architecture based on the phase conjugate holograms (PCH). The novel PCH technique can be used in both wavelength- and angle-multiplexing. Compared with conventional holographic systems for high-density data storage applications, the PCH greatly reduces the systems size, simplifies the architecture, increases the image resolution, reduces the bit error rate, making it a more attractive approach for Tbit/s capacity and Gbits/second transfer-rate optical memories.

articleTitle: 3-D metallic photonic bandgap structures
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Most of the work on photonic bandgap materials to date has focused on dielectric structures because of their low loss at optical wavelengths. While metals are not suitable for use in this range, they find many applications at microwave frequencies. We believe we have constructed the first 3-D metallic photonic bandgap structure in a geometry resembling covalently bonded diamond.

articleTitle: All-optical demultiplexer/inverter using a semiconductor laser amplifier in a single-arm interferometer
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. We present the first demonstration, we believe, of all-optical switching using a semiconductor nonlinearity in a single arm interferometer (SAI). The SAI is insensitive to long-lived nonlinearities and, with a minor modification, allows for generalized logic functions without the use of an additional control stream. We have demonstrated a 10-Gb/s demultiplexer and inverter using an semiconductor laser amplifier in a SAI. Bit-error-rate measurements have been performed and power penalties of 1.7 dB and 3 dB were obtained for demultiplexing and inverting, respectively. We are investigating the scalability of this device to higher rates.

articleTitle: Light extraction efficiency from visible light-emitting diodes
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Because escape probability is about 2% per radiating surface, it is a good idea to use all six emitting surfaces of a solid rectangular LED. We introduce a photonic gas model for modelling this type of LED. Light extraction efficiency in thick (250/spl times/250/spl times/250 /spl mu/m) transparent substrate LED is a result of competition of light escape from the semiconductor chip, reabsorption in the active layer, and free-carrier absorption in the bulk. This modelling is confirmed by Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Multiple wavelength generation in a picosecond optical parametric oscillator based on noncritically phase-matched LiB/sub 3/O/sub 5/
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. The Ti:sapphire laser pumped based on noncritically phase-matched LiB/sub 3/O/sub 5/ (LBO) has been shown to be a versatile source of high-repetition-rate picosecond pulses for the near-infrared. It is capable of providing signal and idler output pulses with durations of 1-2 ps over the continuous wavelength range 1-2.5 /spl mu/m. Here we present results that demonstrate that this system is also capable of directly producing visible picosecond pulses in the green spectral region.

articleTitle: High-order harmonic generation in large molecules and atomic clusters
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Our recent studies of the soft x-rays produced from the intense irradiation of large atomic clusters (100-10,000 atoms per cluster) suggested that these clusters, which form in the adiabatic expansion of a gas jet into vacuum, may be a unique medium for high-order harmonic generation. We have studied the characteristics of the harmonic generation from these clusters and found that, unlike small molecules, clusters can dramatically affect the behavior of the high-order harmonics. We have carefully compared the harmonics generated in single atoms with those produced from clusters with intense, 100-fs laser pulses.

articleTitle: Photocurrents generated by moving optical interference patterns in photoconductive semiconductors in the presence of interband optical excitations
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. When two monochromatic optical fields interfere inside photoconductive semiconductors containing deep level recombination centers, the spatially inhomogenous optical intensity pattern causes the redistribution of photo-excited free charge carriers, resulting in the formation of an internal space charge electric field. The photoconductive semiconductor used was a Si sample with polished but not Ar-coated surfaces.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic generation in silica fibers poled via internal electrodes
publicationTitle: Summaries of papers presented at the Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics
abstract: Summary form only given. Silica fibers exhibiting high second-order nonlinearities (SON) could be used to develop a new generation of all-fiber electro-optic modulators, switches, tunable filters, and frequency converters. A typical fiber used in our experiments had 0.32 NA, 3 /spl mu/m-core diameter, 125-/spl mu/m outer diameter, 50-/spl mu/m hole diameter, and 9-/spl mu/m interhole spacing.
